previous_statement: Uniform norm-one diagonal and cb norm control. For a dagger-preserving T as in node 1.2, at each n and ||X||=1 the defect estimate applied to X^dagger,X gives ||T_n(X)||^2=||T_n(X)^dagger T_n(X)||<=||T_n(X^dagger X)||+a. Taking the supremum M_n=||T_n|| gives M_n^2<=M_n+a, hence M_n<=1+2a for a<=1; thus ||T||_cb<=2. For every finite-dimensional C*-algebra B, normalized Haar measure on its compact unitary group gives the algebraic diagonal D=int U^dagger tensor U dU. In finite dimension it is a finite convex combination D=sum_s p_s U_s^dagger tensor U_s, so sum_s ||p_s U_s^dagger||||U_s||=1; Haar invariance gives XD=DX and multiplication(D)=I. This norm-one representation is independent of dim B. For any bilinear cb defect G of S, the formula w'(x)=sum_s S(p_s U_s^dagger)G(U_s,x) has ||w'||_cb<=||S||_cb||G||_cb; at level n the identical formula with I_n tensor U_s is entrywise I_n tensor w', because the diagonal identity moves arbitrary matrix entries. Therefore every correction below is one level-one map with uniform amplified bounds.
new_statement: Uniform cb control, exact unitalization, and the norm-one diagonal. At each n and ||X||=1, dagger preservation and the defect estimate give ||T_n(X)||^2<=||T_n(X^dagger X)||+a, so M_n=||T_n|| satisfies M_n^2<=M_n+a and hence ||T||_cb<=2 for a<=1. Fix a state phi on B and define S_0(x)=T(x)+phi(x)(I-T(I)). States have cb norm one and phi(x^dagger)=conj(phi(x)), so S_0 is dagger-preserving, exactly unital, ||S_0-T||_cb<=a, ||S_0||_cb<=3, and direct expansion gives multiplicative defect b_0<=c_u*a with the numerical universal c_u=7. For every finite-dimensional C*-algebra B, normalized Haar measure on its compact unitary group gives D=int U^dagger tensor U dU. In finite dimension D is a finite convex combination sum_s p_s U_s^dagger tensor U_s with projective norm one; Haar invariance gives XD=DX and multiplication(D)=I. For a defect G of S, w'(x)=sum_s S(p_s U_s^dagger)G(U_s,x) satisfies ||w'||_cb<=||S||_cb||G||. At level n the same formula is entrywise I_n tensor w', because the diagonal identity moves arbitrary matrix entries. Thus every correction is one level-one map with bounds independent of n and all dimensions.
